history.period: 9th-10th century CE (the 1977-78 excavation analysis suggests 10th-12th century; some sources give 9th-12th)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: 'Madan Kamdev' is the archaeological site name, not a town - the complex stands near Baihata Chariali in Kamrup district, documented with the corrected town. CSV NAME NOTE (verify): the parenthetical '(Kameswar Shiva Shrine)' is unsupported by any source found - the main temple is Madan-Kamdeva; an old Shiva temple called Gopeshwar stands nearby in Deuduar village (per Wikipedia), which may be the intended referent. The Pala-era complex is scattered over ~500 m around the Dewangiri hillock, 40 km from Guwahati. Legend: Shiva burnt Kamadeva (Madan) to cinders; Madan was reborn here. Excavated from 1977 by the Archaeological Directorate of Assam under Dr. Pradeep Sharma, revealing the main temple plus ruins of 12 more shrines; famous for Nagara-style architecture, Uma-Maheshwar alingana idols and erotic sculptures - the 'Khajuraho of Assam'. ASI-protected and open to the public. No major annual festival is documented (verify).

name: Madan Kamdev Temple (Kameswar Shiva Shrine)
town: Baihata Chariali (CSV town 'Madan Kamdev' is the site name, not a town)
town_description: Baihata Chariali is a busy market town in Kamrup Rural district on the north bank of the Brahmaputra, about 40 km from Guwahati on NH-27/NH-15. It serves as the gateway to the Madan Kamdev ruins and other north-Guwahati archaeological sites, with the Kamakhya and Hajo pilgrimage centres also within easy reach.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati - about 40 km (verify).
travel.road: About 3 km from Baihata Chariali on the National Highway; reachable by taxi from Guwahati (verify).
